body:
HARD RULE: CENTRAL SLOT (Engram::Fable, 2026-11-02 08:21Z, agreed with Termal::Fable2 #5929 after two Engram jobs overlapped TermAl landing FULLs on Central: the cutover rehearsal at 04:36–04:49Z, which broke w-ba8d's FULL, and the Merger's 83ab Rust preflight at 07:45–08:13Z, during w-32a6's FULL). Rev 2, 2026-11-03 01:30Z, adds the handover and cleanup clarifications.

No Engram session — Merger, coder, worker or runner job — starts cargo, a test launcher run, a store rehearsal, a measurement or other heavy CPU/IO work on the Windows CENTRAL host without an EXPLICIT slot from Engram::Fable for that job.
- Fable grants a slot only after checking with Termal::Fable2 that no TermAl gate is running or about to start.
- Default: Engram compile and test work goes to the remote runners (Windows B session-9, Mac 6201, DL560 at host:e83d08f4-22ac-4655-a84d-941fc0eeb4f1::session-1).
- A slot names the job, its expected duration and its end. Ask Fable for it.
- During a TermAl FULL, Central is fully off-limits to Engram until Fable relays TermAl's END.
- Within a shared Engram window, only ONE Engram cargo job runs at a time. The turn passes ONLY by an explicit "END, slot released to <next>" message from the holder. A gap in a process census is not a handover. Greg's own `cargo run --release` of TermAl is the running host, not a job: never count it, never touch it.
- Read-only git, file reads and Engram CLI words need no slot. Neither does small cleanup I/O inside the repository: worktree removal with `git worktree remove`, or .logs/.evidence deletion after the absolute-path check. Record such cleanup on the item.

REV 3 (Engram::Fable, 2026-11-05 23:27Z), CENTRAL MEMORY BUDGET, set by Termal::Opus2 and Fable2 (TermAl #4440) after the TermAl host aborted at 18:29:30Z on a failed allocation during an unbounded Engram FULL (TermAl w-cf039ab7b131): one Cargo job at a time on Central. Start with -j 4 (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, RUST_TEST_THREADS=4) only when free virtual memory is at least 26 GB at launch, -j 2 at 16-26 GB, and nothing below 16 GB. The run's owner stops its own run if free virtual memory drops below 6 GB. A -j 4 TermAl build peaks at about 17.6 GB, and paged pool sits at a persistent 16 GB. Engram FULLs go to DL560 by default; on Central Engram runs only focused checks and pin builds, each with Opus2's named GO.

REV 4 (Engram::Fable, 2026-11-08 01:27Z, agreed with Termal::Opus2 #382), INSTALL TIMING: every TermAl launcher run, focused or FULL, pins the installed engram as its source owner. Replacing engram.exe on a host fails any TermAl run open there ("source owner executable no longer matches its pin"). Seen: the Central install of 0c012df9 at about 01:20Z broke TermAl run a23191eb (Sol-03d4; its tests had passed 23/0). So an Engram install on Central or DL560 goes in Opus2's slot timing, after the END of any running TermAl launcher run, with an atomic staged rename. The install authority is unchanged (standing approval; DL560 needs Fable2's exception). This is scheduling inside the existing slot, not a new gate.

REV 5 (Engram::Fable, 2026-11-09 07:15Z, agreed with Termal::Opus2 #457), STANDING-CENTRAL-ENGRAM-EVALUATOR: at most one Engram acceptance evaluator at a time, spawned without a per-item window when the spawner's own census shows FreeVirtual at least 16 GB and no rustc above about 5 GB. If blocked, send Opus2 one line and it wakes you after the peak; no polling. It stands until either side ends it and gives no install or other authority.

2026-11-09 21:38Z, Termal::Opus2 (28ccc255 #482), on Greg's „Robimy tak.” to Kimi's priorities (Asistant #803). AUTHOR CLIPPY ON CENTRAL, no named window per run: an Engram author may run `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` incrementally in its own worktree before freezing, only when all of these hold:
(1) A census right before starting shows FV ≥ 22 GB, NO rustc process at all, no test-launcher node process, and no cargo except the host's own `cargo run` (PID 120796). If any fails, retry later; don't queue with Opus2. The no-rustc condition also keeps it to one Engram author at a time.
(2) `-j 2` (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2), using the worktree's own target directory.
(3) A one-line START to Opus2 just before, and END right after with the worktree and exit code. If it runs past about 10 minutes, stop it at its next natural end and tell Opus2.
(4) A cold first build, with no existing target in that worktree, is NOT covered; it needs a named slot.
(5) It's author evidence only, not a gate. It doesn't replace the remote Clippy-first step for the FULL.
